summary: IDS feed s067_single is degraded: 36.3% of TCP sessions are one-way (62/171), exceeding 10% threshold. IDS requires bidirectional traffic for stateful inspection. All other visibility checks healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker / SPAN is delivering only one direction for a large subset of flows. Most likely cause is SPAN configured RX-only/TX-only, TAP placement on single link of asymmetric path, or broker policy/filter forwarding only one side without aggregating both directions to this IDS port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP reassembly and state tracking. With 36.3% one-way sessions the IDS cannot reconstruct streams, will miss exploits, C2 and data exfiltration that require both sides, and will generate incomplete session logs/false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate client->server and server->client for each flow to the same IDS tool port so the IDS sees complete bidirectional sessions for detection. Verify SPAN/TAP covers both directions and broker aggregation policy forwards both sides together.
